definitions.definition: I={i in Z : 0 <= i <= lambda}. Nonnegative indices and factorial arguments are identified with their natural-number values.
For i in I, e_i=(1/i!) y^i v, where y^0 is the identity and powers mean composition.

definitions.definition: For each integer r>=0, X_r=x^r/r!, with X_0 the identity.

definitions.definition: For each integer r>=0, Y_r=y^r/r!, with Y_0 the identity.

definitions.type: subring of Q, embedded in C by the usual rational embedding
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b in Q : a,b in Z, b != 0, p does not divide b}, with the inherited operations.

M_R is the R-span of M inside V: its elements are finite sums of r m with r in R and m in M. The natural multiplication map R tensor_Z M -> V sends r tensor m to r m. The definition by the image does not assume injectivity of this map.
For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique complex-linear operator with E_ij e_j=e_i and E_ij e_k=0 for every k in I different from j, extended linearly using the complex basis e.
Pi=Y_lambda X_lambda; juxtaposition of operators means composition with the rightmost operator applied first.
J={c in C : c v belongs to M_R}. No generator of J is selected in this definition.
V(K)=M tensor_Z K, with its K-vector-space structure on the K factor.

definitions.type: map from complex-linear endomorphisms T of V preserving M to K-linear endomorphisms of V(K)
definitions.definition: For a complex-linear T with T(M) subset M, red(T) is induced by its integer-linear restriction to M: red(T)(m tensor c)=T(m) tensor c for m in M and c in K, extended K-linearly. This is the tensor extension of an integer-linear map. Expressions red(T) are used only after T(M) subset M is established. The reduced generators in the target are red(x), red(y), red(h).

binders.type: complex-linear endomorphism of V preserving M

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0 <= lambda < p.

n=lambda+1>0, I has n elements, dim_C V=n, and (e_i)_{i in I} is a complex basis of V, with e_0=v. For every integer t>=0, h y^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v; for t>=1, x y^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^{t-1}v. All y^t v vanish for t>lambda. The matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1<=i<=lambda, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0<=i<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i. For every i in I and r>=0, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r<=i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these divided-power coefficients are integers.

Multiplication R tensor_Z M -> V, s tensor m -> s m, is injective with image M_R. M_R is free over R of rank n and spans V over C. Every X_r and Y_r (r>=0) preserves M and M_R; x,y,h preserve M and M_R, so their reductions are defined. For all i,j in I, Pi=E_{lambda,lambda}, X_{lambda-i} Pi=E_{i,lambda}, Pi Y_{lambda-j}=binom(lambda,j) E_{lambda,j}, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R, and E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_{lambda-i} Pi Y_{lambda-j}. Consequently every E_ij preserves M_R.

output.statement: For each i in I the R-module {c in C : c e_i in M_R} equals J. The R-module J is finitely generated and nonzero. The map J^I -> M_R taking (c_i) to sum_{i in I} c_i e_i is an R-linear isomorphism, with inverse the tuple of complex coordinates in the basis e; in particular M_R is the internal direct sum of the modules J e_i.

binders.type: family of elements of J indexed by I

locals.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
locals.declaration: Define J_i={c in C : c e_i belongs to M_R}, for i in I.

argument.text: Define the coordinate modules J_i as stated. N001 gives e_0=v and H001 ensures 0 is in I, so J_0=J. N002 says every E_ij preserves M_R. If c belongs to J_j, applying E_ij to c e_j gives c e_i in M_R, so J_j is contained in J_i. Reversing i,j proves equality; thus all equal J. For any z in M_R, its coordinate projection E_ii z lies in M_R, so every coordinate lies in J. Conversely a finite sum sum_i c_i e_i with all c_i in J lies in M_R. By independence in N001 the representation is unique. These are inverse R-linear coordinate and summation maps, proving M_R is the internal direct sum of J e_i.

produces.statement: Every J_i equals J, and the summation map J^I -> M_R, (c_i) -> sum_i c_i e_i, is an R-linear isomorphism with inverse the e-coordinate tuple.

argument.text: By N002, M_R has a finite R-basis. Its coordinate map at index 0 has image J by F001, so the finitely many 0-th coordinates of that basis generate J. This explicitly proves finite generation. Moreover M_R spans the nonzero space V (N001 gives positive dimension). Therefore some element of M_R has a nonzero coordinate in the basis e. That coordinate lies in some J_i=J by F001, proving J is nonzero. Together with F001 this proves the entire coordinate-decomposition statement.
